claim: Home Assistant's MQTT integration publishes a birth message 'online' to homeassistant/status when the MQTT integration starts, and devices using MQTT discovery must subscribe to this topic and re-send their discovery payload in response to restore entities after HA restarts.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent must implement birth-message-triggered discovery re-publish to be reliable across HA restarts
scope_conditions: Home Assistant MQTT integration, current documentation
quoted_support: When MQTT starts up, all existing MQTT devices, entities, tags, and device triggers, will be unavailable until a discovery message is received and processed. A device or service that exposes the MQTT discovery should subscribe to the Birth message and use this as a trigger to send the discovery payload. To avoid high IO loads on the MQTT broker, adding some random delay in sending the discovery payload is recommended.

claim: On HA restart, discovered MQTT items with a unique_id become unavailable until a new discovery message is received; items without a unique_id are not added at all at startup.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent discovery messages must carry unique_id and be re-offered after MQTT integration (re)start
quoted_support: When Home Assistant is restarting, discovered MQTT items with a unique ID will be unavailable until a new discovery message is received. MQTT items without a unique ID will not be added at startup.

claim: Retained discovery messages are an alternative to birth-triggered rediscovery, but they can create ghost entities that keep coming back, and HA supports the MQTT 5 Message Expiry Interval to bound retention.
stance_target: agent should combine retained discovery with message expiry to avoid both unavailability and ghost entities
scope_conditions: HA MQTT discovery; MQTT 5 broker support required for expiry
quoted_support: A disadvantage of using retained messages is that these messages retain at the broker, even when the device or service stops working. They are retained even after the system or broker has been restarted. Retained messages can create ghost entities that keep coming back.

claim: MQTT entity availability is configured per-entity via availability topic(s) with payload_available ('online' default) / payload_not_available ('offline' default), and availability_mode (all/any/latest) controls when an entity is marked online.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent should publish a retained availability topic per device with online/offline payloads and set LWT with the broker
quoted_support: A device or service can announce its availability by publishing a Birth message and set a Will message at the broker. When the device or service loses connection to the broker, the broker will publish the Will message. This allows the MQTT integration to make an entity unavailable.

claim: The last_reported attribute of MQTT entities only updates when force_update is set, because MQTT state updates are often repeated with no change.
stance_target: agent telemetry design: repeated identical state publishes do not update last_reported unless force_update is used
quoted_support: MQTT devices often continuously generate numerous state updates. MQTT does not update last_reported to avoid impacting system stability unless force_update is set.

claim: Home Assistant explicitly does not support ActiveMQ or the RabbitMQ MQTT plugin as brokers because they break MQTT message retention; Mosquitto is the recommended broker.
stance_target: jupiterOS fleet should standardise on Mosquitto for the agent's broker
quoted_support: Neither ActiveMQ MQTT broker nor the RabbitMQ MQTT Plugin are supported, use a known working broker like Mosquitto instead. There are at least two issues with the ActiveMQ MQTT broker which break MQTT message retention.

claim: Enabling a previously disabled entity more than 30 seconds after startup causes the MQTT integration to reload and unload all discovered MQTT entities.
stance_target: fleet-scale caveat: entity enable operations trigger full discovery reload
quoted_support: If a disabled entity is enabled and added after 30 seconds, the MQTT integration will be reloaded and will cause all discovered MQTT entities to be unloaded.
